answer: Let n attackers mirror a cluster, each committing capital C with quadratic slashing s(C)=kC^2 plus comet liquidity sinks. The marginal attack cost is sum kC_i^2, which scales super-linearly with n as O(n^2) for equal stakes. Any extracted value V is bounded by protocol fees and finality premiums, so V <= alphaC + beta. Choosing k, alpha, beta yields k n^2 > alpha + beta for all n, making marginal cost exceed value and voyage risk subeconomic.
